exposition_resources.author: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown

exposition_resources.author: James Strong
exposition_resources.excerpt_text: Strong's lexical entries for creation terms note purposeful formation and ordering, supporting a theological reading centered on God's intentional design rather than randomness.

exposition_resources.author: William Smith

day_briefs.day_title: Romans 5:2-3 - We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ
day_briefs.focus_clause: We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ
day_briefs.pastoral_burden: peace with God received through justification by faith alone
day_briefs.scene_summary: Romans 5:2-3 opens with a scene marked by peace with God received through justification by faith alone.
day_briefs.theological_lane: justification by faith alone gives the sinner standing, peace, and access to grace that no human effort could earn or sustain
day_briefs.application_lane: joyful hope in the glory of God that flows from peace with him, received by faith alone and not by effort added to what Christ finished
forbidden_drifts: generic encouragement detached from the scene
applications that ignore the specific burden of the passage

day_briefs.day_title: Romans 5:5-6 - At the right time Christ died for the ungodly
day_briefs.focus_clause: At the right time Christ died for the ungodly
day_briefs.pastoral_burden: hope that holds firm because Christ died for the helpless before they deserved it
day_briefs.scene_summary: Romans 5:5-6 opens with a scene marked by hope that holds firm because Christ died for the helpless before they deserved it.
day_briefs.theological_lane: hope rooted in suffering does not shame the believer because God's love was proved by Christ dying for the ungodly before any merit existed
day_briefs.application_lane: hope-filled endurance that rests on Christ who died for the helpless before they deserved it, not on strength that suffering tests
forbidden_drifts: generic encouragement detached from the scene
applications that ignore the specific burden of the passage
flattening severe themes into comfort language

day_briefs.day_title: Romans 5:9-10 - If while we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son
day_briefs.focus_clause: If while we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son
day_briefs.pastoral_burden: reconciliation with God received while we were still enemies
day_briefs.scene_summary: Romans 5:9-10 opens with a scene marked by reconciliation with God received while we were still enemies.
day_briefs.theological_lane: God reconciled his enemies to himself through Christ's death and keeps them by his risen life, making boasting in God the proper response
day_briefs.application_lane: bold rejoicing in God through Christ, who reconciled enemies by his death and saves them by his life without waiting for them to become worthy

day_briefs.day_title: Romans 5:16-17 - On the other hand the free gift arose from many transgressions resulting in justification
day_briefs.focus_clause: On the other hand the free gift arose from many transgressions resulting in justification
day_briefs.pastoral_burden: the free gift of righteousness that far exceeds the reach of the transgression
day_briefs.scene_summary: Romans 5:16-17 opens with a scene marked by the free gift of righteousness that far exceeds the reach of the transgression.

day_briefs.focus_clause: Even so grace would reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord
day_briefs.pastoral_burden: grace that abounded more than sin through the obedience of the one man
day_briefs.scene_summary: Romans 5:19-20 opens with a scene marked by grace that abounded more than sin through the obedience of the one man.
